name: Micah
bio:
Micah was a man from the hill country of Ephraim. He had stolen eleven hundred shekels of silver from his mother, who had pronounced a curse over it; when Micah confessed and returned the silver, his mother said she had already dedicated it to the LORD to make a carved and cast idol for her son, and gave two hundred shekels of it to a silversmith, who made the idol and placed it in Micah's house (Judges 17:1-4). Micah set up a shrine of gods in his house, made an ephod and household idols, and installed one of his own sons as priest (Judges 17:5).

A young Levite later passed through, and Micah hired him as his personal priest, promising ten shekels of silver a year plus clothing and food (Judges 17:7-12). Spies from the tribe of Dan recognized the Levite's voice when passing through Micah's house; later, six hundred armed Danites came through, took the carved idol, the ephod, and the household gods from Micah's house, and persuaded the Levite to come along as priest for the entire tribe of Dan. Micah pursued and protested, but was powerless against their numbers and had to turn back home (Judges 18:1-26). Micah's story reflects the chaos of the era when "there was no king in Israel" and "everyone did as they saw fit," and shows how setting up private idol worship ultimately ends in loss.
